concepts.def: The traditional system of classification, developed by Carl Linnaeus, in which living things are classified into groups depending on their structure and characteristics.

The groups Linnaeus classified living things into: kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus and species. Kingdom is the largest group and species the smallest, so organisms placed in the same genus share more characteristics than organisms placed only in the same class.
The system used to name organisms, in which an organism is given a two-part name made up of its genus followed by its species, for example Panthera leo.

Classification systems proposed after Linnaeus. As evidence of internal structures became more developed due to improvements in microscopes, and the understanding of biochemical processes progressed, new models of classification were proposed.

The system developed by Carl Woese, due to evidence available from chemical analysis, in which organisms are divided into Archaea (primitive bacteria usually living in extreme environments), Bacteria (true bacteria) and Eukaryota (which includes protists, fungi, plants and animals).
A method used by scientists to show how they believe organisms are related, drawn using current classification data for living organisms and fossil data for extinct organisms.

mcqs.q: A student is given the names of two organisms: Panthera leo and Panthera pardus. Which Linnaean group is given by the shared name Panthera?
options: Their order in the Linnaean system
Their family in the Linnaean system
Their genus in the Linnaean system
Their species in the Linnaean system
mcqs.explain: Organisms are named by the binomial system of genus and species, so the first part of each name, Panthera, gives the genus that the two organisms share.

mcqs.q: Linnaeus classified living things depending on their structure and characteristics. Why were new models of classification later proposed?
options: Because much larger numbers of species were discovered
Because improved microscopes showed internal structures
Because fossils of many extinct organisms were discovered
Because bacteria were found in many extreme environments
mcqs.explain: As evidence of internal structures became more developed due to improvements in microscopes, and the understanding of biochemical processes progressed, new models of classification were proposed.

mcqs.q: In the three-domain system developed by Carl Woese, into which three groups are organisms divided?
mcqs.explain: Due to evidence available from chemical analysis, organisms are divided into Archaea, Bacteria and Eukaryota, with protists, fungi, plants and animals included in Eukaryota.
